test_focus: statistical-power re-run of Phase 10 + 11 — N=20 trials per scenario per domain with parallelized API calls. Goal: tight 95% Wilson confidence intervals on the treatment win rate by domain, after Phase 12's variance findings showed N=7 was too small to draw firm conclusions.
tester: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context), live as the developer

experiment_design.per_trial_agent_ids: phase14-<domain>-s<scenario_idx>-t<trial_idx> so concurrent trials don't race on snapshot writes
experiment_design.judge_blinding: response order randomized per trial via seeded RNG
experiment_design.judge_prompts: domain-specific (technical favors unblocking + tool-naming; creative favors non-obvious angle + memorable framing)

technical.interpretation: Statistically significantly BELOW 50% — treatment hurts on technical-debugging prompts. The 95% CI [21%, 36%] does not include 50%, confirming the directional finding from Phase 10.

creative.interpretation: Statistically significantly ABOVE 50% — treatment helps on creative/design prompts. The 95% CI [72%, 85%] does not include 50%, confirming Phase 11's headline at much tighter precision.

results.domain_effect_size: Treatment win rate differs by 51 percentage points between domains (79% creative vs 28% technical). The 95% confidence intervals do not overlap. This is one of the largest and most robust effect sizes in the campaign.

implications: **The domain-conditional effect is now statistically robust at N=140 per domain.** The technical CI [21%, 36%] and the creative CI [72%, 85%] do not overlap. Treatment differs by 51 percentage points between domains — this is the single biggest and most reliable finding in the campaign.

**Phase 10's headline (1/7 wins on technical) UNDERSTATED the technical win rate. Phase 12's 5/7 OVERSTATED it. The true value is ~28% — both prior runs were within reasonable N=7 noise of this number.** Phase 14's N=140 finally pins the magnitude.

**Phase 11's headline (6/7 wins on creative) was an OVERESTIMATE of the true 79%, but in the right ballpark.** N=7 favored the high-margin side of the noise; Phase 14 confirms the directional finding with much tighter precision.

**The shipped context-aware routing (Phase 11/12 commit) is justified by this data.** Engineering agents getting the neutral wrapper avoids the ~28% treatment-win rate; creative agents getting the dreams wrapper gets the ~79% lift.

**Per-scenario heterogeneity is REAL.** Technical scenarios range from 10% (retry-under-load) to 55% (legacy-deletion) treatment-win. Creative scenarios range from 70% to 90%. Even within a domain, some scenarios are friendlier to imagination injection than others. The legacy-deletion scenario sits near the 50% line on the technical side — suggesting it has some creative / decision-flavored qualities that the heuristic classifier could pick up.
**Cost is reasonable.** $2.10 for 840 API calls over 4 minutes 15 seconds wall clock — well within reach for any future statistical-power phase.

feature_verdicts.imagination_injection_on_creative_prompt: SINGS — 79.3% win rate (95% CI [72%, 85%]) at N=140
feature_verdicts.imagination_injection_on_technical_promp: HURTS — 27.9% win rate (95% CI [21%, 36%]) at N=140; the shipped neutral-wrapper routing addresses this
feature_verdicts.domain_conditional_effect: ROBUST — 51 pp difference between domains, non-overlapping 95% CIs

known_limitations: per-scenario heterogeneity isn't fully explained — legacy-deletion at 55% may be a creative/decision-flavored question masquerading as technical
verdict: DECISIVE — domain-conditional effect is statistically robust. The shipping context-aware routing is justified by data, not just intuition.
next_steps: Phase 15 (running): test whether engineering-craft seeds beat computing-history seeds on technical prompts. Hypothesis: domain-appropriate content might lift treatment from 28% to closer to 50%.
Phase 16 (suggested): LLM classifier fallback for the long tail of profiles that the keyword classifier returns 'general' on.
Phase 17 (suggested): per-call routing — classify the prompt, not just the agent. For agents that span domains.
